question:
Refer to the exhibit. An engineer installs a new Cisco UCS B-Series server. The requirement is to install an operating system on a LUN that is provided by the Fibre Channel storage array.
Which two steps must be configured in the boot policy to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)
context: UCS Manager GUI: Create Boot Policy dialog. Fields: Name, Description, Reboot on Boot Order Change, Enforce vNIC/vHBA/iSCSI Name (checked), Boot Mode (Legacy/Uefi). Boot Order sections: Local Devices, CIMC Mounted vMedia, vNICs, vHBAs, iSCSI vNICs, EFI Shell. Boot Order table columns: Name, Order, vNIC/vHBA, Type, LUN Na..., WWN, Slot No..., Boot No... (No data available).
options: Add Local CD/DVD and SAN Boot.
Set Boot Order to External USB and LAN Boot.
Create iSCSI vNICs and add Local LUN.
Configure a SAN Boot Target with a WWPN.
theory: A boot policy for booting from a Fibre Channel array LUN needs both a local boot device to start the media (Local CD/DVD, e.g., for OS install media) and a SAN Boot entry, and that SAN Boot entry must be paired with an explicit boot target defined by the storage array's WWPN so the server's vHBA knows which target/LUN to boot from. Options describing USB/LAN boot, iSCSI vNICs with a local LUN, or disabling name enforcement do not establish a Fibre Channel SAN boot path, which is why adding Local CD/DVD + SAN Boot and configuring a SAN Boot Target with a WWPN are the two required steps. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Storage Management, SAN Boot Policy Configuration)
